title: How Rome Took The Mediterranean
tts: TTS unavailable (ClientConnectorDNSError: Cannot connect to host speech.platform.bing.com:443 ssl:<ssl.SSLContext object at 0x7f6f84) -> silent render + narration files for CapCut

lines.text: One small city in Italy grew into an empire that ruled the entire Mediterranean.
lines.visual: map: year=264 BC | view=italy>empire | cities=Rome | label=Rome rises

lines.text: Then it fought Carthage, in North Africa, for over a century.
lines.visual: map: year=264 BC | view=west_med | route=Rome > Carthage | label=The Punic Wars

lines.text: In 218 BC, Hannibal marched elephants over the Alps and nearly broke Rome.
lines.visual: map: year=218 BC | view=west_med | route=Carthago Nova > Pyrenees > Alps > Po Valley > Cannae | label=Hannibal's march

lines.text: Rome won anyway. By 133 BC, it held Spain, North Africa, and Greece.
Julius Caesar then added Gaul, today's France.
At its peak in 117 AD, the empire stretched from Britain to Egypt.
lines.visual: map: year=117 AD | view=wide>empire | label=Greatest extent | note=Shown by modern country. Borders approximate.

lines.text: Tens of millions of people lived under Roman rule.
lines.visual: stat: label=People under Roman rule | value=50–70M | sub=Common scholarly estimate at its peak
